canonicalFacts.statement: The ward assemblies choose their own officers.

story.title: The Missing Ward
story.premise: Surveyor Iven finds a salt-stained ledger whose record of an inhabited ward was scraped away.
story.conflict: Correct the public census or trust anonymous witnesses who fear official enumeration.
story.motivation: Iven's childhood ward will lose its flood rations.
story.opposition: The Salt Hall clerks demand a public list of names.
story.background: Ward assemblies ration salt and dry shelter by the last census.
progression: Compare flood marks at the gate.
possibleEndings: Restore the roll at Salt Hall.
Keep a witness register at the beacon.

coverage.reason: The scraped ledger is the central evidence.
Authority comes from the ward assemblies.

story.title: Borrowed Tide
story.premise: A ledger of borrowed sluice-hours exposes two wards promised the same stretch of low tide.
story.conflict: Spend the last opening on this harvest or use it to flush silt for next year.
story.motivation: Iven wants both wards to survive the winter.
story.opposition: A salt growers' compact insists on immediate access.
story.background: Sluice time functions as currency on the tidal flats.
progression: Fly tide kites above the flats.
possibleEndings: Save the harvest and carry the debt.
Rebuild the channel through a lean season.

coverage.reason: Conflicting time loans appear on facing ledger pages.
Authority comes from the ward assemblies.

story.title: The Last Survey
story.premise: Iven must carry a ledger of abandoned names on the final survey before a valley is surrendered to the sea.
story.conflict: Move the memorial inland or let every village reclaim its own page.
story.motivation: Iven promised displaced families a say in what survives.
story.opposition: An inland archive will accept only an undivided volume.
story.background: Each village marks a final dry-season walk through its old streets.
progression: Deliver the book or distribute its pages.
possibleEndings: Return each page to its village.

coverage.reason: The ledger is both the travel itinerary and the disputed memorial.
Authority comes from the ward assemblies.
